canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the prevailing usage treats interpretability and explainability as human-understandability of a model's internals, learned features, or decision process: representations, sparse features, concept layers, retrieved evidence, and reasoning traces count as interpretable when humans can inspect them, trace outputs to supporting sources, or give concise explanations of activations. A sizable minority uses explainability more narrowly for rationales, critiques, or other justifications that accompany predictions or judgments, sometimes contrasted with systems that provide only labels or numerical scores, while a smaller group uses transparency for inspectable embedding dimensions or identifiable knowledge sources. The main axis of variation is what is being made understandable, internal mechanisms and representations versus output-level rationales, evidence traces, or source attributions.

Space of facets. Papers often place interpretability, explainability, and transparency under the same umbrella, and some explicitly pair the labels or treat interpretability and explainability as interchangeable. At the same time, they carve out narrower variants, such as feature-level and model-level forms, mechanistic interpretability, intrinsic variants, and human auditability, with additional labels for weights, reward processes, and algorithms. These variants differ mainly by target: some focus on human-readable latents or embedding dimensions, others on internal states or circuits, and others on stepwise evaluation, decision traces, or rationales; feature-level work also ties the construct to monosemantic or disentangled components.

Space of measurement. Operationalization is diverse: papers link the construct to 10 measurement instruments and 17 behavioral indicators. The most common instruments are Automated interpretability, LLM-as-a-judge, Human evaluation, SAEBench, and CUB-200-2011, plus five others. In practice, studies use automated classification or benchmark scores for sparse autoencoder features, ask LLM judges or human raters whether latents, reasoning paths, or generated outputs are understandable, and use datasets with human explanations or concept annotations; some also score explanations with plausibility and faithfulness. Together, these measures cover both internal-feature understandability and output-level justification.

Links. Several papers claim a causal relationship from Reasoning to this construct, and smaller strands make parallel causal claims from Chain of thought and Explanation generation. In the other direction, papers most often claim a causal relationship from interpretability and explainability to Trustworthiness and Controllability. Other papers report additional causal links to task-specific outcomes, one paper reports a correlation with task performance, and a few papers describe it as related to several further constructs and behaviors.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the prevailing usage treats interpretability and explainability as human-understandability of a model's internals, learned features, or decision process: representations, sparse features, concept layers, retrieved evidence, and reasoning traces count as interpretable when humans can inspect them, trace outputs to supporting sources, or give concise explanations of activations. A sizable minority uses explainability more narrowly for rationales, critiques, or other justifications that accompany predictions or judgments, sometimes contrasted with systems that provide only labels or numerical scores, while a smaller group uses transparency for inspectable embedding dimensions or identifiable knowledge sources. The main axis of variation is what is being made understandable, internal mechanisms and representations versus output-level rationales, evidence traces, or source attributions.

characterization_sections.label: Space of facets.
characterization_sections.text: Papers often place interpretability, explainability, and transparency under the same umbrella, and some explicitly pair the labels or treat interpretability and explainability as interchangeable. At the same time, they carve out narrower variants, such as feature-level and model-level forms, mechanistic interpretability, intrinsic variants, and human auditability, with additional labels for weights, reward processes, and algorithms. These variants differ mainly by target: some focus on human-readable latents or embedding dimensions, others on internal states or circuits, and others on stepwise evaluation, decision traces, or rationales; feature-level work also ties the construct to monosemantic or disentangled components.

characterization_sections.label: Space of measurement.
characterization_sections.text: Operationalization is diverse: papers link the construct to 10 measurement instruments and 17 behavioral indicators. The most common instruments are Automated interpretability, LLM-as-a-judge, Human evaluation, SAEBench, and CUB-200-2011, plus five others. In practice, studies use automated classification or benchmark scores for sparse autoencoder features, ask LLM judges or human raters whether latents, reasoning paths, or generated outputs are understandable, and use datasets with human explanations or concept annotations; some also score explanations with plausibility and faithfulness. Together, these measures cover both internal-feature understandability and output-level justification.

characterization_sections.label: Links.
characterization_sections.text: Several papers claim a causal relationship from Reasoning to this construct, and smaller strands make parallel causal claims from Chain of thought and Explanation generation. In the other direction, papers most often claim a causal relationship from interpretability and explainability to Trustworthiness and Controllability. Other papers report additional causal links to task-specific outcomes, one paper reports a correlation with task performance, and a few papers describe it as related to several further constructs and behaviors.

definition_agreement.reason: Most papers define the construct as human-understandability or transparency of a model's internal mechanisms and decisions, but many others use it for different targets such as the quality of generated explanations or rationales, the human-meaningfulness of learned features or code, or even an evaluation method's ability to give reasons. Because these definitions place the property on different kinds of things and would often lead papers to study different phenomena, the overall pattern is conflicting.
